children: For the first time in its nearly 32 years of existence, HDFC Bank will have an outsider helming its operations. ICICI Group veteran Anup Bagchi will be the new Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer of India’s largest private sector bank.

RBI approved HDFC Bank’s application for the appointment of Bagchi, currently serving as Chief of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, as MD & CEO of the Bank for three years with effect from October 27, 2026.

The announcement relating to the new appointment comes in the wake of Sashidhar Jagdishan deciding not to seek re-appointment for a third term as the MD & CEO of HDFC Bank amid controversy that started with the abrupt resignation of the Bank’s Part-Time Chairman in March 2026.

Sashidhar has been helming HDFC Bank since October 27, 2020, and his term ends on October 26, 2026. Aditya Puri headed the Bank for the longest period — since incorporation in 1994 till October 26, 2020. So, Bagchi will be the Bank’s third chief in 32 years.

Kaizad Bharucha, Deputy Managing Director (DMD), HDFC Bank, was believed to be a strong contender for the top position at India’s largest bank, and now it is not clear if he will continue to stay on with the bank. He has been on the Bank’s board since 2014.

HDFC Bank, in a regulatory filing, said Bagchi, who has been a member of the ICICI Group since 1992, has built a diverse career spanning treasury, retail banking, wholesale banking, investment banking, and digital financial services.

The Bank noted that over the course of his career, he has held several pivotal leadership positions, including CEO & MD of ICICI Securities, Executive Director of ICICI Bank, and currently MD & CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.

“Bagchi’s vast experience across the financial services space at ICICI Bank should hold him in good stead while he helms India’s largest private-sector bank. It is a huge responsibility to steer a domestic systemically important bank such as HDFC Bank,” said a market expert.
The street probably had an inkling about the new appointment as the bank's stock bucked the broader market weakness to end 1.36 per cent higher to ₹719.35 on BSE.

title: ICICI Group veteran Anup Bagchi to head HDFC Bank
